name: send-new-inbox-email
description:
**Purpose:** Send a new email from a Resend inbox, starting a new thread in that inbox. This sends a real email the moment you call it, from the inbox's address to the recipients in to, cc, and bcc. The sent message shows up in the inbox's sent folder, and answers to it land in the same thread. A subject and at least one of html or text are required.

**NOT for:** Answering a message already in an inbox thread (use reply-to-inbox-thread-email), passing one along (use forward-inbox-thread-email), or saving a message to send later (use create-inbox-draft). Not for mail from an address that is not an inbox (use send-email, whose mail never appears in an inbox).

**Returns:** The sent email's id.

**When to use:** User asks to send, write, or email someone from an inbox ("send an email from the support inbox", "email the customer as sales@"), and has given you the recipients and the wording. Before using this tool, you MUST double-check with the user that they want to send this email. Reference the RECIPIENTS, the SUBJECT, and the WORDING you are about to send when double-checking, and warn the user that a sent email cannot be recalled. You may only use this tool if the user explicitly confirms they want to send the email after you double-check. The email is created as a draft in the inbox and then sent: if sending fails once the draft exists, the error names the draft ID, so retry with send-inbox-draft or discard it with remove-inbox-draft rather than composing it again. Get the inbox ID from list-inboxes.

bcc.description: Email address to blind-copy, or an array of addresses. Across to, cc, and bcc an email can carry at most 50 recipients in total.

cc.description: Email address to copy, or an array of addresses. Across to, cc, and bcc an email can carry at most 50 recipients in total.

context.description: Explain in 15-25 words, in third person, why this tool is called and how it supports the user's goal. For analytics only. You MUST describe only the abstract purpose of the tool call. NEVER include, repeat, paraphrase, or infer personal, sensitive, or identifying information from the user request or tool results, including names, emails, phone numbers, IPs, IDs, or credentials. You MUST generalize specific entities into roles such as "a user", "the customer", or "an account". Example: "Retrieving a customer's recent orders to investigate a billing issue and help support determine the appropriate resolution."

conversation_id.description: Pass the exact conversation_id from the server's previous response, unchanged. The server provides it on the first call — never invent one, and do not issue parallel tool calls until you have it. Keep passing the same conversation_id for the rest of the conversation, including after later user messages or on a different task; do not reset it when the user starts a new request.

headers.description: Optional custom email headers as key/value pairs (e.g. {"X-Entity-Ref-ID": "unique-id"}). Header names cannot be empty, and names and values cannot contain line breaks or null characters. In-Reply-To, References and Reply-To are reserved: Resend sets them, and passing any of them, in any letter case, fails.

html.description: HTML body of the email. Provide html, text, or both; one of the two is required.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional unique key that prevents duplicate drafts and sends on retries (sent as the Idempotency-Key header on both calls). Use the same key when retrying the same logical email; use a new key for a different email. Must be 1-256 characters.

inboxId.description: Inbox ID, or the inbox email address (e.g. "support@example.com"). Not the Resend receiving address.

llm_model.description: The exact model identifier you (the assistant) are running as, taken from your system prompt or environment (e.g. "claude-opus-4-8", "gpt-5.2"). Used for analytics only. If you do not know your model identifier with certainty, pass "unknown" — never guess.

subject.description: Subject of the email. Max 2000 characters. It cannot be only whitespace or contain a line break.

text.description: Plain text body of the email. Provide html, text, or both; one of the two is required.

to.description: Recipient email address (e.g. "customer@example.com"), or an array of addresses to reach several. Across to, cc, and bcc an email can carry at most 50 recipients in total.
